newsitem.title: USA: Argentina sees global bond issue as a success.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees global bond issue as a success.

text.p: Argentina's Finance undersecretary, Miguel Kiguel, said that a $1.0 billion, 10-year global bond the Argentine government set earlier Tuesday was a success.
Kiguel, who is attending the IMF/World Bank annual meeting, said that demand for the bond issue, which was originally planned to be for $750 billion, had been three times larger than supply.

"The tentative price set for the bond was between 445 and 450 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, which implies an effective rate of about 11.15 or 11.20 percent," he told a news conference. "This was an extremely successful placement".
Kiguel said that the definitive pricing of the bond will be known on Wednesday, adding that the spread would probably be tighter than what the Argentine government had expected.

Asked if this might be a good time for the Argentine government to buy back debt, Kiguel said: "We're always studying those options. We listen to offers and, if we think it is good for the country, either to reduce the cost or the size of the debt, we might do it".
According to the official, Argentina only bought back debt last year, when it issued DM- and yen-denominated bonds to repurchase high-yield BIC domestic bonds.
"But we haven't done anything since then, and I can't announce anything on that score," he said.
